title.official: Liability of litigation representative for costs

division.heading: Other Matters Related to Lawyers’ Charges and Litigation Costs

operative_text.controlling:
10.47(1)  A litigation representative for a plaintiff is liable to pay a
costs award against the plaintiff.
(2)  A litigation representative for a defendant is not liable to pay a
costs award against the defendant unless
(a) the litigation representative has engaged in serious
misconduct, and
(b) the Court so orders.

BOOK_A.title: Liability of Litigation Representative for Costs
BOOK_A.commentary:
In complex receivership, where the court had to supervise, the court refused to allocate costs
based on the proportion of debt owed to each creditor to the total debt owed by the debtor. That
proposal would have made the creditor who would get the least from the option bear the largest
proportion of costs. The two secured creditors should not bear more than their pro rata share of
allocated costs.¹
The litigation representative of a minor plaintiff, the named plaintiff in a class action by minors,
got exemption from paying costs of the upcoming certiﬁcation motion.²
BOOK_A.operative_text_note: same as official operative text (EXACT_MATCH); see operative_text_sha256
BOOK_A.commentary_review_flag: Read in full, p.10-137 (line 7358) to p.10-138 (line 7382): title (line 7358), rule text (lines 7359-7365; no footnote marker, no amendment bracket), the Information Note (lines 7366-7368: 'For rules about litigation representatives see Part 2 [The Parties to Litigation] Division 2 [Litigation Representatives].'), the marker 10-138 (line 7370) and running head (line 7371), Related Provisions (lines 7373-7374: '2.11 (litigation representatives) ; 2.14(2) (f) (acknowledgment of liability for costs).', with a full stop at the end), the note (two paragraphs, lines 7376-7380 with marker '1' and lines 7381-7382 with marker '2') and 2 footnotes: p.10-138 fn 1 (line 7411, Re Respec Oilﬁeld Serv. 2010 ABQB 277 (Apr 28)) and fn 2 (line 7412, L. C. v. R. (Alta. ) 2015 ABQB 713, JCE 0703 10836 (Nov 7)); fns 3 and 4 and the history of that block belong to 10.48. Read against the official text: the rule text equals official 10.47 (EXACT_MATCH, no differences); the Information Note is printed in Book A (and in a garbled copy in Book C); the official text has no such note; its references land: official Part 2 is 'The Parties to Litigation' (line 89 of the table of contents) and the litigation representative rules are 2.11 to 2.14 and following. (1) Related Provisions: '2.11 (litigation representatives)' is a label for official 2.11 'Litigation representative required'; '2.14(2) (f) (acknowledgment of liability for costs)' does not land: official 2.14(2)(f) is 'if the litigation representative is a corporation, the place of business or activity of the corporation in Alberta'; the acknowledgment of potential liability for a costs award is 2.14(2)(g). The same pointer '2.14(2) (f)' is printed in the Rule 2 note (combined_rule2.txt line 1555). (2) The note's statements read against the rule: 'In complex receivership, where the court had to supervise, the court refused to allocate costs based on the proportion of debt owed to each creditor to the total debt owed by the debtor ... The two secured creditors should not bear more than their pro rata share of allocated costs' (fn 1, Re Respec Oilfield Serv. 2010 ABQB 277) is about allocating costs among creditors in a receivership and does not concern the liability of a litigation representative under 10.47; 'The litigation representative of a minor plaintiff, the named plaintiff in a class action by minors, got exemption from paying costs of the upcoming certification motion' (fn 2, L. C. v. R. (Alta.) 2015 ABQB 713) is an exception to official 10.47(1) (a litigation representative for a plaintiff is liable to pay a costs award against the plaintiff), which has no exception clause; fn 2 has the file number 'JCE 0703 10836', which is also the file number of 'L. C. v. Child Welfare (#_) 2023 ABKB 334, JCE 0703 10836' in the 10.34 note (p.10-123 fn 1, line 6713), so the two footnotes name the same proceeding differently ('L. C. v. R. (Alta.)' and 'L. C. v. Child Welfare'). (3) No supra or infra is used; no '(#_)'-type placeholder in the two footnotes ('(Alta. )' is Book A's court label). The rule has no history footnote, so no old-rule references. Book B has no commentary for this rule (its 2.11/2.14 commentary cites r 10.47 in rule2_part02_document.json), so nothing in this note is corroborated by Book B.
